Week 12 Waiver Wire 2026 Week 12 Preview: SMU Mustangs @ Notre Dame Fighting Irish DALLAS, TX - NOVEMBER 14: SMU Mustangs head coach Rhett Lashlee leads his team on to the field during the Atlantic Coast Conference college football game between the SMU Mustangs and the Wake Forest Demon Deacons on November 14, 2026, at Gerald J. Ford Stadium in Dallas, TX. (Photo by Matthew Visinsky/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Steve Helwick · SB Nation Thu, November 19, 2026 at 4:51 PM UTC · 9 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Time and date: Saturday, November 21 at 7:30 p.m. ET Location: Notre Dame Stadium — South Bend, IN Spread: Notre Dame (-20.5) Over/under: 56.5 All-time series: Notre Dame leads, 10-3 Last meeting: Notre Dame 59, SMU 6 — November 11, 1989 Current streak: Notre Dame, 3 (1986-89) Setting the scene How does SMU respond to a loss? Especially a rare home defeat in which the Mustangs trailed 42-0 at halftime and effectively watched their ACC championship aspirations evaporate? The Mustangs have responded with tremendous poise under head coach Rhett Lashlee, who has not dropped consecutive regular season matchups since his inaugural campaign in 2022. But this isn't just any follow-up matchup. Immediately after facing 9-1 Wake Forest, SMU must travel to South Bend and take on another 9-1 opponent in Notre Dame. SMU just suffered its first regular season defeat without holding a second half lead since 2023. Now, the Mustangs enter Saturday's matchup as three-touchdown underdogs against one of the nation's premier programs. A chance to deliver the ultimate bounce-back statement awaits at Notre Dame Stadium. SMU Mustangs outlook Nov 14, 2026; Dallas, Texas, USA; SMU Mustangs safety Ahmaad Moses (7) during the game between the Mustangs and the Demon Deacons at Gerald J. Ford Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Last Saturday, SMU (7-3, 5-3 ACC) endured a series of unwanted firsts. The Mustangs lost their first-ever ACC matchup at home. The Mustangs suffered their first-ever home loss in ACC play and their first conference defeat by more than 10 points, falling 49-7 to Wake Forest after an uncompetitive first half. The road to redemption won't get any easier against Notre Dame. However, the potential reward is even greater than last week's setback, as SMU can secure its first victory over an AP Top 5 opponent since defeating No. 2 Texas in 1980. Program icon Kevin Jennings looks to author a signature performance before exhausting his eligibility. The fifth-year senior quarterback ranks seventh nationally in passing yards, sitting 27 yards shy of his third-straight 3,000-yard season. He's also fifth in the country with 26 passing touchdowns. Most impressively, Jennings operates with some of the highest efficiency in the FBS. His 62.9 completion rate last week was his lowest of the season, and he ranks third nationally, connecting on 72.6 percent of attempts. SMU's 15th-ranked offense can be as dynamic and explosive as any in the country, but that was not the case last week when it registered just 47 yards across its first six possessions. Wake Forest largely eliminated the Mustangs' run game from the onset, forced early turnovers, and provided significant pressure on dropbacks. Part of the challenge has been integrating a revamped offensive line. SMU recently inserted two true freshmen into starting roles on the left side while retaining veterans Joshua Bates, Addison Nichols (who is questionable), and PJ Williams at center, right guard, and right tackle, respectively. That unit faces a formidable test against Notre Dame's defensive front. The Mustangs' rushing attack has been volatile this season. Starting running back Kendrick Raphael has eclipsed 100 yards three times in ACC play, but there were three other conference games where the entire ground game was held below 70 yards, including last week. Raphael remains the workhorse tailback, but freshman Christian Rhodes has gotten increasingly involved, generating 92 rushing yards two weeks ago against Virginia Tech. SMU features an abundance of capable playmakers in its receiving corps. Four Mustangs have at least 30 receptions on the season, led by Yamir Knight's 56 catches for 670 yards and six touchdowns. Yannick Smith and Jalen Cooper are among other downfield threats, while tight end Randy Pittman Jr. has been a consistent intermediate target all season. This group supplies much of the offense's explosive potential, helping SMU rank fifth nationally with seven 50+ yard completions this season. The Mustangs only surrendered more than 30 points once before last week. The defensive line had proven overwhelming against several ACC opponents, but Wake Forest managed to neutralize that advantage. SMU ranks 20th nationally and third in the conference with 2.8 sacks per game, spearheaded by Marques White. The eighth-year senior defensive end leads all ACC defenders with 8.5 sacks, while adding 12.0 tackles for loss, two forced fumbles, and two fumble recoveries in a standout season. SMU struggled containing the run game last week, and the defense has been middle-of-the-road in that department this year. The passing defense, meanwhile, has made significant strides since 2025, although it recently experienced a major setback. Safety Jimmy Wyrick is out for the year, joining Tyren Polley Jr. as the second starting safety to suffer a season-ending injury. However, reigning First Team All-ACC selection Ahmaad Moses, who was granted an injunction for temporary eligibility, will make his second appearance of the season after debuting against Wake Forest. Moses had five interceptions last year, including two against SMU's most recent top-10 opponent, Miami (FL). As heavy road underdogs at Notre Dame, SMU can't just rely on stops. The Mustangs need to ramp up their turnover output after producing just three interceptions in their first 10 games. Notre Dame Fighting Irish outlook SOUTH BEND, IN - NOVEMBER 07: Notre Dame Fighting Irish offensive lineman Anthonie Knapp (54) in action during a college football game between the Miami Hurricanes vs Notre Dame Fighting Irish on November 07, 2026 at Notre Dame Stadium in South Bend, IN. (Photo by Jeffrey Brown/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Notre Dame (9-1, Independent) is continuing its College Football Playoff pursuit after missing the field in 2025. The Fighting Irish secured a signature win Nov. 7 against otherwise-undefeated Miami (FL), staving off a late comeback to put themselves in prime playoff position. Outside of close finishes against current top-10 opponents Miami (FL) and BYU, the Fighting Irish have demolished the competition. Their other eight victories all came by double-digits, and North Carolina was the only other opponent to finish within 17 points. Following off a 34-point annihilation of Boston College, Notre Dame currently ranks first in point differential against FBS opponents at +25.6 per game. Quarterback CJ Carr enjoyed a promising debut season last year, but the junior has taken another significant step forward in 2026. His completion percentage has ballooned to 67.9, his passing yards per game output has climbed by 10, and he has delivered an efficient 24 touchdowns against two interceptions. Given the lopsided nature of most Notre Dame games, the quarterback hasn't been shouldered with a heavy load in second halves. But when he needed to come through against Miami (FL), he did with a season-high 319 passing yards along with three touchdowns. Carr is supported by the wide receiver duo of Jordan Faison and Micah Gilbert, who are nearly identical in production this season. Faison has 615 receiving yards and six touchdowns, while Gilbert presents 614 yards and six scores. Recently, Gilbert has taken command of the offense, recording 14 receptions for 184 yards and three touchdowns across his last two starts. That doesn't mean Faison has faded into the background, and he found the end zone in both of those ACC victories. Replicating last year's run game was never going to be easy after losing two first-round NFL Draft picks, but the Fighting Irish are steadily reestablishing an identity on the ground. They produced a 100-yard rusher in four of their last six outings. Much like the receiving corps, the running back room is driven by a duo with similar statistics and similar builds. Jonaz Walton has 655 rushing yards on the season, and he's been the more explosive with 7.0 yards per carry. Meanwhile, Nolan James Jr. follows closely with 644 rushing yards, and his 10 touchdowns are tied for 18th in the country. But the underlying catalyst for Carr and the run game's success is arguably the best offensive line in the country. Notre Dame ranks first nationally in fewest sacks allowed, surrendering just three through 10 games. The line, anchored by potential All-American gaurd Anthonie Knapp, has also surrendered the fewest tackles for loss and yardage from tackles for loss in the FBS. As dominant as Notre Dame's seventh-ranked scoring offense has been, its fifth-ranked scoring defense has been equally as imposing. The Fighting Irish surrender just 13.8 points per game and lead the FBS in total defense, allowing a mere 240 yards per contest. Only three teams managed more to score more than 13 points against this unit — BYU (28), North Carolina (26), and Miami (FL) (24). Although Notre Dame hasn't generated sacks at the highest rate, its defensive front has consistently disrupted opposing quarterbacks. Defensive end Boubacar Traore leads the charge with 5.0 sacks, 8.0 tackles for loss, and three forced fumbles, while his counterpart Bryce Young has registered 4.0 sacks and 6.5 tackles for loss. The Fighting Irish will be shorthanded at the next level, however, as inside linebacker Drayk Bowen remains out for the third-straight game. Rounding out an imposing defense is reigning unanimous All-American cornerback Leonard Moore. After intercepting five passes last season, Moore has yet to record a pick in 2026. That doesn't mean opposing quarterbacks have found success targeting him. Rather, his presence has deterred passers from looking in his direction, and he has done a standup job locking up WR1s all season. Even against one of the highest-ranked opponents on the road, it is nearly impossible for things to go worse for SMU than they did last week. The Mustangs should enter South Bend with renewed urgency and considerably more competitiveness on both sides of the ball, keeping the matchup within reach through several quarters. However, the Mustangs will need to find production in multiple areas to remain competitive. Notre Dame holds significant advantages elsewhere, particularly in the trenches. Notre Dame makes the playoff if they win out, but a dominant win would be even more helpful. Location : Notre Dame Stadium (Notre Dame, Ind.) Date : Saturday - November 21 Time : 7:30 PM ET Networ k: NBC/Peacock Here are our staff predictions for the game: Prediction : Notre Dame 38, SMU 17 Some of the magnitude of this game was diminished when SMU lost to Wake Forest last weekend in a blowout (49-7). SMU is a much better football team than it showed against the Demon Deacons, and that game reminded me a lot of Notre Dame's loss to Miami in 2017. It was one of those games that just got away from them early, but make no mistake, SMU is a dangerous football team. Notre Dame will need to play at a high level, because I expect SMU to come out looking to make an early statement and bounce back from their bad loss last weekend. The key for Notre Dame will be coming out early and jumping all over the Mustangs. They will need to quickly take away SMU's confidence and not let their potent offense get into any kind of rhythm. That will require the defense to be turned loose and be allowed to attack quarterback Kevin Jennings . If they are allowed to do that, and if the DL handles business, they will force Jennings to make mistakes, and that's how Notre Dame rolls in this game. My prediction is based on SMU being able to make some plays early due to their impressive talent at wide receiver and the fact Jennings is a dangerous player. I expect the Irish defense to quickly get up to speed and slow SMU down over the final two quarters. On the other side of the ball, Notre Dame will look to establish the run game early and get Nolan James Jr . and Jonaz Walton to get going. They will look to soften the Mustangs up and that's when CJ Carr should get rolling and pick the Mustangs apart. If the offensive line handles business the Notre Dame offense should have a big day and the Irish should roll. If Carr gets going early the offense could be extremely difficult to stop in this matchup. Prediction : Notre Dame 41, SMU 13 This is the final of three major tests for the 6th ranked Notre Dame Fighting Irish. SMU is coming off a 49-7 loss to Wake Forest at home during their own Senior Day matchup, but don't let that fool you, this is still a talented team making the trip up north. But like a lot of their opponents for the 2026 season, this matchup is more about Notre Dame living up to its potential than it is about facing an opponent that's superior. As it was said best in Wednesday's show, Marcus Freeman needs to know 'what time it is' in college football. SMU is a quality opponent, but not good enough that simply winning the game will boost their resume all on its own. I expect the Fighting Irish offense to come out firing early. Quarterback CJ Carr will hit some big plays early. The biggest question, will Notre Dame keep their foot on the gas after jumping out to an early lead? I think they answer that to a degree, but Freeman needs to learn from the lessons he's experienced in the previous two seasons. I have the Irish winning by 28 on Senior Day. I'm picking Notre Dame to win convincingly against SMU, but this game is about more than simply adding another win to the schedule. With the College Football Playoff committee evaluating every result, the Irish need to make a statement and show that they belong among the nation's elite. Notre Dame cannot afford to play down to its competition or let SMU hang around into the second half. This is an opportunity to dominate on both sides of the football, establish the running game, stretch the field offensively, and demonstrate the kind of physical superiority that separates playoff contenders from everyone else. The Irish need to take care of business, but they also need to make it look impressive. SMU has enough offensive talent, particularly with quarterback Kevin Jennings , to make things interesting if Notre Dame allows it. However, coming off a 49-7 loss to Wake Forest, the Mustangs are vulnerable, and Notre Dame needs to take full advantage. I want to see the Irish defense create turnovers, get after Jennings, and keep SMU from finding any offensive rhythm. More importantly, Notre Dame needs to keep its foot on the gas rather than become conservative with a comfortable lead. The committee won't just see another win but it will see how the Irish perform against an opponent they are expected to handle. This is a chance to deliver a dominant performance, build momentum, and send a message that Notre Dame is a legitimate national championship contender. Prediction : Notre Dame 52, SMU 13 Before last weekend, I was going to pick a closer game (something like 38-24), but a combination of both the SMU blowout loss to Wake Forest and Notre Dame's dominant win over Boston College made me reconsider. First, I was pleased that the Irish played the attacking style of defense against Boston College that we saw for the second half of 2025, early in 2026, and then again against Miami. I don't think SMU's offensive line can hold up against the Irish front-seven when they play aggressively. The Mustangs gave up three sacks and six tackles for loss to Wake Forest, and rank 96th in the country in sacks allowed in road games this season. Getting SMU behind the sticks is going to put the onus on Kevin Jennings to make plays. He is really talented, but has a penchant for putting the ball in danger and making a few of those "what is he doing" kind of plays per game. There's a reason that SMU ranks 118th in the country in turnover margin at -6, and Notre Dame ranks 2nd at +16. Also, whether its due to corruption, malice, or just plain incompetence, there are no guarantees for Notre Dame when it comes to the CFP Committee. Marcus Freeman knows that it's not enough to just win these final two games - the Irish need to be dominant if they want to secure a home playoff game. With Wake Forest having such a big win last weekend over SMU - in Dallas no less - I think that will force Freeman and the Irish to keep the pedal down more than would be typical on a Senior Day when the staff typically tries to get all seniors a couple snaps once the game is in hand. Notre Dame's offense should not have much trouble moving the ball against a Mustangs defense that was blitzed by the two best offenses it faced (giving up 488.5 YPG against ranked opponents), and I think the Irish send a message on the scoreboard. Prediction : Notre Dame 35, SMU 10 SMU is a rising program, no question, which was why I was definitely surprised to tune into the game in the second half on Saturday to see such a lopsided score against Wake Forest. The Demon Deacons hammered SMU, leaving them off the scoreboard in the first half and quickly lighting up the scoreboard. While the Mustangs can certainly compete with anybody and Saturday's score was definitely out of character with how their season has gone, I don't think Notre Dame will have much trouble with them, provided they get off to a good start and play disciplined football. It really feels like Mike Denbrock has found his groove, with a great mix of run-and-pass with CJ Carr and Notre Dame's three-headed monster in the backfield: Jonaz Walton , Nolan James Jr. and Aneyas Williams . Give me the Irish.

Mandatory Credit: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Josh Ortega · SMU Mustangs On SI Fri, November 20, 2026 at 6:59 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads DALLAS - The SMU Mustangs (7-3, 5-3 ACC) face one of their toughest road trips of the season this weekend. The Mustangs will travel to South Bend to face the No. 5 Notre Dame Fighting Irish (9-1) Saturday night at the historic Notre Dame Stadium. The Mustangs haven't traveled to South Bend since the late 1980s. SMU holds a 1-6 record against the Fighting Irish on the road. Notre Dame leads the all-time series 10-3 overall. SMU faces a tall task after being routed in their first ACC loss at Gerald J. Ford Stadium in over three years. The Mustangs were drilled by No. 13 Wake Forest 49-7 last week. The Demon Deacons outgained SMU 535-275 while holding the Mustangs to 209 passing yards and 69 total rushing yards. As a result, SMU's chances of heading to Charlotte for the ACC championship game and a potential shot at the College Football Playoff have grown slimmer. SMU Head Football Coach Rhett Lashlee spoke during this week's media availability on his team's performance last week and the challenge that this week presented to bounce back. "Life's about opportunities, we had one last week we didn't take advantage of it. We have done a good job of taking advantage of our opportunities here. We did not put our best foot forward last week," said Lashlee during Tuesday's media availability. "Sometimes when that happens if we were playing someone that we were expected to beat or what not. I don't know what you gain from that, but having the opportunity to go on the road against an elite opponent we know it's going to take our very best to beat regardless of what happened last week. I like that it's a great opportunity, a great challenge, and we get to see what we are made of and how we respond to that opportunity." Notre Dame has been a top team in college football this season. After famously being left out of the College Football Playoff last season, Head Football Coach Marcus Freeman and his team have gone to work to ensure the Fighting Irish don't leave any boxes unchecked for a guaranteed ticket to the postseason. The Irish are 9-1 through 10 games with a staple win over the ACC leader and former No. 1 team in the country, the Miami Hurricanes, atop their season resume. Notre Dame leads the nation in the fewest yards allowed to opposing offenses. While boasting one of the nation's best offenses. Junior quarterback C.J. Carr is top 10 in passing touchdowns this season with 23, while being among the top 25 in total passing yards with 2,385 this season. Carr has been in the Heisman conversation all season in his second season as a starter. He has only been intercepted twice and sacked three times this season. He is coming off a 200-yard performance against Boston College, after throwing for a season-high 319 yards against Miami. The second-year starter has a veteran pair of wide receivers bolstering the passing attack. Senior wide receiver Jordan Faison leads the receiver room with 615 yards on 49 catches with six scores. Not far behind him is junior receiver Micah Gilbert, who has recorded 614 yards on 38 grabs with six of his own scores this season. Fellow senior Jaden Greathouse is also a reliable weapon for Carr this year, securing 25 catches for 354 yards after dealing with injury for most of last season. The multiple weapons for the home team will be a massive test on the SMU's secondary. After losing both star running backs to the NFL, Notre Dame's rushing attack has been bolstered by a pair of young stars with only 11 yards separating them. Freshman running back Jonaz Walton leads the team in rushing yards with 655 yards this season, averaging 7.0 yards per carry this season with five scores. The true freshman ran for over 140 yards and a score in Notre Dame's 41-7 win over Boston College last week. Sophomore running back Nolan James Jr. is second on the team in rushing yards with 644. The second year back has had more than 120 attempts running the football this season, with a knack for finding the end zone. James Jr. has scored 10 times so far this season, the most on the roster. SMU allowed 286 rushing yards with 6.4 yards per carry against Wake Forest last week. The Mustangs will have one of the most talented backfield duos in the country rushing at them Saturday night. Lashlee went on to describe Notre Dame's style of play as methodical and patient, yet still able to be explosive. "The way they play allows them to be patient, methodical, and just wear on you," said Lashlee. "Because of their talent they create explosive plays, but they are not necessarily wired where they have to. They have no problem going on 10, 12, 13 play drives and just wearing on you. So that's what you worry about over the course of the game." SMU gears up for one of its toughest tests of the season Saturday in a game that has been circled on the calendar since the schedule was released. away.headline: Notre Dame loses Luke Talich for the remainder of the 2026 season after devastating Achilles injury during win over SMU
away.source: A to Z Sports on MSN
away.blurb: Notre Dame suffered another big injury blow against SMU. Star safety Luke Talich is out for the remainder of the 2026 CFB season. The 6-foot-4, 222-pound safety from Cody, Wyoming, arrived in South Bend as a preferred walk-on despite having several Power Four offers coming out of the 2023 class. He wasn't a highly touted recruit coming out of high school as he should have been, but he steadily worked his way up the depth chart and earned a scholarship in the spring of 2024. The return of Brauntae Johnson helps, but it doesn't erase the loss Getting a player of his caliber back is enormous. Johnson was expected to be one of the leaders of this defense entering the season, and his return gives the Irish another experienced option at safety. Notre Dame now has to figure out how to replace a player who had become an important piece of its defensive identity. Starter Adon Shuler and Joey O'Brien are among the options available, but losing Talich's production, experience, and versatility changes the complexion of the position group. Johnson's return helps soften the blow. It doesn't make losing Talich any less significant. The recovery process typically involves surgery, immobilization, progressive weight-bearing, extensive rehabilitation, and eventually a return to football-specific activities. Unfortunately, the timing makes it difficult to envision Talich being ready for the beginning of the 2027 season. A return at some point during that season is possible, but Notre Dame and Talich will have to be patient with the recovery. Talich has an additional year of eligibility available under the NCAA's five-for-five eligibility structure. That means he could potentially return to Notre Dame for the 2027 season if he decides that is the best path forward. It creates a fascinating decision. Does Talich enter the draft and bet on the evaluation he built throughout his senior season? Or does he return to Notre Dame, complete his rehabilitation and give NFL teams another opportunity to evaluate him at full strength? Notre Dame's victory over SMU came with a significant price. Multiple sources have confirmed that senior safety Luke Talich suffered a ruptured Achilles during the Fighting Irish's game against the Mustangs on Saturday, November 21, ending his 2026 season and dealing another frustrating blow to a Notre Dame secondary that has already had to navigate its fair share of injuries. The injury occurred on SMU's opening possession. Talich made an impressive play in the end zone, breaking up a pass intended for tight end Theo Melin-Ohrstrom . Unfortunately, he was unable to get up and walk off the field under his own power. Talich was eventually helped to the sideline, where he was seen wearing a walking boot on his right leg and using crutches. The initial images were concerning, and the confirmed Achilles diagnosis makes the situation even more difficult to swallow. Notre Dame has a 99% chance to make the College Football Playoff and a 16% chance to win

home.headline: Notre Dame loses Luke Talich for the remainder of the 2026 season after devastating Achilles injury during win over SMU
home.source: A to Z Sports on MSN
home.blurb: Notre Dame suffered another big injury blow against SMU. Star safety Luke Talich is out for the remainder of the 2026 CFB season. The 6-foot-4, 222-pound safety from Cody, Wyoming, arrived in South Bend as a preferred walk-on despite having several Power Four offers coming out of the 2023 class. He wasn't a highly touted recruit coming out of high school as he should have been, but he steadily worked his way up the depth chart and earned a scholarship in the spring of 2024. The return of Brauntae Johnson helps, but it doesn't erase the loss Getting a player of his caliber back is enormous. Johnson was expected to be one of the leaders of this defense entering the season, and his return gives the Irish another experienced option at safety. Notre Dame now has to figure out how to replace a player who had become an important piece of its defensive identity. Starter Adon Shuler and Joey O'Brien are among the options available, but losing Talich's production, experience, and versatility changes the complexion of the position group. Johnson's return helps soften the blow. It doesn't make losing Talich any less significant. The recovery process typically involves surgery, immobilization, progressive weight-bearing, extensive rehabilitation, and eventually a return to football-specific activities. Unfortunately, the timing makes it difficult to envision Talich being ready for the beginning of the 2027 season. A return at some point during that season is possible, but Notre Dame and Talich will have to be patient with the recovery. Talich has an additional year of eligibility available under the NCAA's five-for-five eligibility structure. That means he could potentially return to Notre Dame for the 2027 season if he decides that is the best path forward. It creates a fascinating decision. Does Talich enter the draft and bet on the evaluation he built throughout his senior season? Or does he return to Notre Dame, complete his rehabilitation and give NFL teams another opportunity to evaluate him at full strength? Notre Dame's victory over SMU came with a significant price. Multiple sources have confirmed that senior safety Luke Talich suffered a ruptured Achilles during the Fighting Irish's game against the Mustangs on Saturday, November 21, ending his 2026 season and dealing another frustrating blow to a Notre Dame secondary that has already had to navigate its fair share of injuries. The injury occurred on SMU's opening possession. Talich made an impressive play in the end zone, breaking up a pass intended for tight end Theo Melin-Ohrstrom . Unfortunately, he was unable to get up and walk off the field under his own power. Talich was eventually helped to the sideline, where he was seen wearing a walking boot on his right leg and using crutches. The initial images were concerning, and the confirmed Achilles diagnosis makes the situation even more difficult to swallow. Notre Dame has a 99% chance to make the College Football Playoff and a 16% chance to win

home.blurb: Two players stood out above the rest. What stands out most about these two is how their roles have evolved. For the longest time, Viliamu-Asa was viewed as a guy who could blitz and handle all sorts of second-level pressures. Now we are seeing that he is a true middle linebacker, and a really good one. Notre Dame injuries have allowed them to redefine its identity Skip to content College Football Close Menu All College Football Notre Dame football's defense looked different against Boston College, and different in a good way. Who earned the defensive game ball for the Fighting Irish? Notre Dame football's defense has taken on a changing identity over the last couple of weeks. Part of that is due to injuries. The other part is the ascension of a couple of different players on that side of the ball. That trend continued in the Fighting Irish's 41-7 victory over the Boston College Eagles. The defense still attacked, just like Irish fans have come to love. It looked different in the best way possible. Notre Dame didn't need five- and six-man pressures to get after the quarterback, and it didn't need to get exotic on the back end to fool anybody. The message was simple: come beat us. Kyngstonn Viliamu-Asa shut down Boston College's best weapon One player who continues to catch my eye every week is linebacker Kyngstonn Viliamu-Asa . He is healthy now, and he keeps getting better and better. KVA finished with seven total tackles, but the box score doesn't come close to telling the whole story. If you watched this game, he was a big reason Notre Dame was able to stifle the Boston College run game early. That run game starts with quarterback Mason McKenzie. He came into the matchup with 676 rushing yards and five touchdowns on the ground. Against the Irish, McKenzie ran the ball 10 times for 14 yards. Credit defensive coordinator Chris Ash and/or head coach Marcus Freeman for that. The plan, at least on a high volume of snaps, was to have Viliamu-Asa shadow and spy the quarterback. Notre Dame essentially told McKenzie he wasn't going to beat them with his legs. KVA was the answer. Here's the thing about McKenzie: if he can't run the football, he can't play. He finished 8-of-21 passing for 51 yards, a touchdown, and an interception. He is a running quarterback, and once Notre Dame took that away, the Boston College offense had nowhere to go. As the new starting middle linebacker, Viliamu-Asa continues to do everything for this team. He can blitz, he can spy, and he can play stacked on the second level. You cannot underrate how important he is. The 6-3, 230-pound linebacker is as dynamic and versatile as anyone on the roster. Luke Talich is all over the field This won't be breaking news to anybody, but safety Luke Talich is awesome. The 6-4, 221-pounder racked up six total tackles, a sack, and a tackle for loss against the Eagles. He was all over the place. Week 12 Waiver Wire Story by Wildcats Wire Kentucky at Missouri: Final thoughts, prediction Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire · Wildcats Wire Sat, November 21, 2026 at 5:31 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky football is facing their final road trip of the season as they travel to CoMo to face off against the Missouri Tigers . We have previewed the explosive Missouri offense and the Tigers' defense that has playmakers at every level. We also detailed the path to victory for the Wildcats to end this two game skid. This is an incredibly intriguing matchup as these are very similar teams in terms of talent and features two teams that have their backs against the wall following back-to-back losses. As we mentioned this week, Kentucky's offensive line is truly the key to this football team and a unit that has to get back to playing at a high level. This offensive line was rewarded for their play that led the Cats to a 7-1 start, which allowed them to be listed as semifinalists for the Joe Moore Award. Over the last two weeks and specifically last week against Florida, they have not lived up to those honors. If Kentucky continues to play like that up front, they are in a very realistic danger of closing out the season on a four game losing streak. The offensive line was the position group Will Stein and his staff invested the most in overall for year one of this new regime, and it is fair to say by doing so they sacrificed other position groups like wide receiver. Kentucky needs the offensive line to be the best position group on the football field, and through eight weeks of the season they were consistently doing so. Expect an incredible effort from this group on Saturday night, they need to give Kenny Minchey time in the pocket and create displacement in the run game. This is where the game is won and lost as we saw last week against the Gators. Another key area is turnovers, which is an area that Kentucky was thriving in through the first eight weeks of the season. Over the last two weeks, the Wildcats have forced zero turnovers on defense and it has led to them being -4 in the turnover margin in those two losses. Slot corner Aaron Gates dropped an interception against Florida that could have swung the momentum of the game. Luckily, they could have those similar opportunities arise against Missouri. Per Clark Brooks, who does his own charting of all SEC teams on secstatcat.com, Austin Simmons has thrown the most passes this season that could have been intercepted. Simmons has faced good turnover luck, as he has just three interceptions on the season. If you look at the trend of Kentucky's wins versus losses in conference matchups, the Wildcats are facing well over 30 pass attempts per games in their five wins while facing just 20 pass attempts per game in their three losses. This could play out in the Wildcats favor, Missouri puts the ball in the hands of their quarterback as Simmons is averaging 30 pass attempts per game on the season. This game will fall on three areas in my opinion: which team wins the line of scrimmage, which team can create turnovers and which team simply wants the win more. This is a true coin flip game, Missouri is much more talented than their record shows. The Tigers had to face a Mississippi State team on the road against a healthy Kamario Taylor, an Ole Miss team that had superstar running back Kewan Lacy and just suffered back-to-back losses to Texas and Georgia. I have had a hard time deciding who wins this game because I really think these teams matchup evenly, but I ultimately think Missouri gets the win at home in an extremely hard fought game. Prediction: Missouri 31, Kentucky 28 This article originally appeared on UK Wildcats Wire: Kentucky at Missouri: Final thoughts, prediction

Week 12 Waiver Wire Story by Wildcats Wire Missouri Defense Preview: Can Kentucky's offense bounce back? Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire · Wildcats Wire Thu, November 19, 2026 at 1:25 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky football travels to CoMo for the final road game of the season against the Missouri Tigers. The Wildcats offense desperately needs to respond after scoring just 20 points in the last two weeks which has led to back-to-back losses. Missouri is a well coached, good all around football team and the defense has been consistent this season. However, the Tigers had their worst defensive performance of the season on the road last week against Georgia. Both teams are coming off back-to-back losses, Kentucky has scored just 20 points on offense in the past two weeks. Conversely, the Missouri defense has allowed 72 points over the last two weeks, albeit to Georgia and Texas. Kentucky has to find some of the offensive success they had before the bye week if they want to finish the season on a strong note. A win at Missouri would give the Wildcats six wins in SEC play, which has only happened once in program history and that was in the 1977 season. I fully expect a motivated performance from both teams to try and put an end to their respective two-game losing streaks. Kentucky's offensive line was named a semifinalist for the Joe Moore Award and have since had to of their worst performances of the season. Last week against Florida was the worst the offensive line has looked all season, so you can almost guarantee they will respond the right way in this game. Quiet frankly, they have to because if the offensive line plays like they did against the Gators they will be in danger of a winless month of November. Missouri's defense has playmakers at every level, but they will allow teams to move the football. Among SEC teams, the Tigers rank 10th in success rate allowed, 7th in pass success rate allowed and 12th in rush success rate allowed. Missouri also ranks 8th in the SEC in EPA/play allowed, 7th in EPA/pass allowed and 12th in EPA/rush allowed. The Tigers have also allowed explosive plays this season, as they rank 14th in the conference in explosive play rate allowed. This will be a difficult matchup for Kentucky, but it starts by winning the line of scrimmage and getting the run game going. The Wildcats averaged just two yards per carry against Florida and had just 61 rushing yards. They will lose this game if they can not turn that around, but the Missouri run defense has struggled at times this season. Kentucky has to stay ahead of the chains and that starts with the run game on early downs, which is something they had been good at all season. We mentioned the Tigers have playmakers at every level of the defense, and that starts up front with edge defender Daeden Hopkins. Hopkins leads the team in sacks (7) and tackles for loss (7.5). Linebacker Nicholas Rodriguez leads the middle of the defense, Rodriguez is a tackling machine with a team-leading 107 tackles on the season; he also has seven tackles for loss and 3.5 sacks on the year. The secondary is led by safety Santana Banner, Banner has 84 tackles on the season, 6 pass breakups and 2.5 tackles for loss. Kentucky has to account for these three players, as they are the strength of this Missouri defense at every level. Hopkins, Rodriguez and Banner have each forced two fumbles this season as well. They have consistently made big time plays for the Tigers all season long. Kentucky has to find ways to exploit this defense and avoid letting these three players make game changing plays. In a lot of ways, this matchup is about Kentucky after scoring just 20 points in the last eight quarters. The offense just is not playing well, and what happened on the line of scrimmage against Florida was alarming. Kentucky has to get the big blue wall back to playing like semifinalists for the Joe Moore Award. This offense lacks explosive plays and yards after contact ability, so they will continue to struggle if the offensive line can't get back to playing at a high level. picks.headline: BY THE NUMBERS: Previewing Kentucky vs. Missouri
How No. 16 Kentucky football and Missouri match up — with a game prediction
picks.blurb: • Kentucky’s Kenny Minchey (68.8% completions, 2,160 yards, 15 touchdowns vs. two interceptions) had a challenging game in UK’s 21-14 upset loss to visiting Florida last week. The 6-foot-2, 211-pound product of Hendersonville, Tennessee, completed only 15 of 26 passes for 181 yards with one touchdown. In going 0-2 since returning from an Oct. 31 open week, Kentucky has allowed too much pressure on its QB. Minchey has been sacked six times and hurried 10 times total in losses to Tennessee and Florida. • Missouri’s Austin Simmons (62.3% completions, 2,379 yards, 21 touchdowns vs. three interceptions) has thrown for seven combined touchdowns in Mizzou’s past three games. A 6-4, 220-pound product of Miami, Simmons has already started a game vs. UK. Playing last season for Ole Miss, Simmons made his first career road start at Kroger Field. The QB threw two early picks as Ole Miss fell behind 10-0. Simmons steadied, however, and threw for 235 yards and ran for 44 yards and a TD as the Rebels rallied to beat Kentucky 30-23. Advantage : Missouri Running backs • UK leading rusher CJ Baxter (562 yards, 5.3 yards a carry, eight touchdowns; 13 catches, 91 yards, one TD) caught a 5-yard touchdown pass in the loss vs. Florida but had a hard time on the ground vs. the Gators. The 6-1, 230-pound product of Boynton Beach, Florida, rushed 8 times for 21 yards vs. his home-state school. Since missing the Oklahoma game due to injury, Baxter has subsequently carried 20 times for 78 yards in the three games. Third-year player Jason Patterson (495 yards, 6 yards a carry, three TDs) had 22 yards on five rushes vs. Florida and caught a pass for nine yards. • Missouri’s Jamal Roberts (1,133 yards, 5 yards a carry, nine touchdowns) is second in the SEC in rushing. A 6-foot, 216-pound St. Louis product, Roberts has run for 100 yards or more in five games this season, and has gone above 200 yards rushing in a game twice. Ahmad Hardy led the SEC in rushing in 2025, running for 1,649 yards and 16 touchdowns. However, the 5-10, 210-pound product of Oma, Mississippi, missed the first seven games this season as he recovered from being shot in the left leg May 10 while attending an outdoor concert in Laurel, Mississippi. Since returning three games ago, Hardy has carried 10 times for 41 yards. Wide receivers • Kentucky freshman Kenny Darby (49 catches, 601 yards, three touchdowns) needs two catches and 29 receiving yards to shatter Barion Brown’s UK freshman marks (50 receptions, 628 receiving yards in 2022) for most catches and receiving yards in a season. Second-year player DJ Miller (26, 324, 1) caught four passes for 80 yards vs. Florida but also had a costly drop on UK’s final offensive possession of the game. • Missouri’s Cayden Lee is second in the SEC in receptions and first in the conference in receiving yards (879). A transfer from Ole Miss, the 5-11, 180-pound fourth-year player has caught at least five passes in every Mizzou game in 2026 other than last week’s 48-21 loss at No. 1 Georgia, when he was held to three receptions for 44 yards. Lee caught one pass for eight yards for Ole Miss in its win at Kentucky last season. Sophomore Donovan Olugbode is also having a big year for Missouri. The 6-2, 210-pound Chicago product has made 47 catches for 691 yards and eight touchdowns. • Kentucky’s Willie Rodriguez is tied for fifth in the FBS in receptions by a tight end with 50. The 6-4, 249-pound, third-year player from Covington Catholic High School has turned those team-high 50 receptions into 467 receiving yards and three touchdowns. A model of consistency, Rodriguez has caught either five or six passes in each of UK’s past six games. • Missouri’s Brett Norfleet has 14 catches for 120 yards and two TDs. The 6-6, 255-pound fourth-year player caught one pass for seven yards in last week’s loss to Georgia. Jude James has averaged 10 yards a catch on his seven receptions. Advantage : Kentucky Offensive line • In the losses to Tennessee and Florida the past two weeks, Kentucky right tackle Malachi Wood has seemed to struggle in pass protection. Of the 6-8, 329-pound Madison Central product, Will Stein said “We all know, I know, (I) think everybody on our team knows (Wood’s) talent level is as good as you’re going to find in the country. It’s just consistency at that position.” • Missouri left tackle Cayden Green is the pillar of a Tigers offensive front that has surrendered the fewest QB sacks (nine) in the SEC. After starting five times for Oklahoma in 2023, Green transferred to Mizzou and started all 13 games in 2024 at left guard. Since switching to left tackle prior to the 2025 season, the 6-5, 324-pound Green has become a standout. So far in 2026, he has not allowed a sack or quarterback hit. Defensive line • Kentucky end Mi’Quise Humphrey-Grace (36 tackles, six sacks, nine tackles for loss, nine quarterback hurries) had a streak of three straight games with at least one sack snapped vs. Florida. Tackle Tavion Gadson (33 tackles, three sacks, five TFL, two pass breakups, two fumble recoveries) also made four stops against the Gators. Gadson has now gone three games without a sack. • Missouri defensive end Daeden Hopkins is fourth in the SEC with seven sacks. The 6-6, 250-pound second-year player has also been credited with 11 quarterback hurries. A transfer from Miami, second-year tackle Donta Simpson has emerged as a disruptor for Eli Drinkwitz and Co. The 6-4, 300-pound Simpson has six QB sacks, 7.5 tackles for loss and eight QB hurries. Advantage : Even • Even though Kentucky MLB Grant Godfrey (13 tackles) and WLB Bo Barnes (nine stops) were UK’s two leading tacklers vs. Florida, the prevailing thought was that UF’s ample success with the QB run game owed, in some part, to the Wildcats’ linebackers not fitting the run properly. “There were some big, big missed tackles in the game that sprung explosive runs by their quarterback,” Will Stein said. “That goes back to us not executing the fundamentals and technique of our position.” • Missouri WLB Nicholas Rodriguez leads the SEC in tackles with 107. The 6-foot, 225-pound Miami product has made at least 11 tackles in eight of Mizzou’s 10 games to date. MLB Robert Woodyard Jr ., a transfer from Auburn, is 22nd in the SEC with 64 tackles and has forced two fumbles and picked off a pass. Defensive backs • Kentucky safeties Jordan Castell and Ty Bryant are tied for second in the SEC in interceptions with four apiece. However, neither has a pick in either of UK’s past two games, the losses at Tennessee and to Florida. Castell, a 6-2, 211-pound product of Orlando, is ninth in the SEC with 76 tackles. Bryant, a 6-foot, 196-pound Lexington native, is 12th in the SEC with 74 stops. • Missouri cornerbacks Sione Laulea and Chris Graves Jr. are tied for second in the SEC with 10 passes successfully defended. Strong safety Santana Banner has recovered two fumbles and broken up six passes. Special teams • Kentucky place-kicker Adam Zouagui is 12 of 15 on field-goal tries with a long make of 52 yards. For the second time this season, UK switched punters vs. Florida. After Wilson Berry punted for four games (averaging 42.6 yards a kick), UK went back to its original starting punter of 2026, Murray State transfer Thomas O’Hara , vs. the Gators. O’Hara kicked three times vs. UF and averaged 46.3 yards a kick. On the season, O’Hara, an Australian, has averaged 41.5 yards on 20 punts. • Missouri place-kicker Blake Craig has missed nine of his 24 field-goal tries this season but has a long make of 53 yards. Craig has been better from outside 50 yards (5 of 7, 71.4%) than from inside 50 yards (10 of 17, 58.8%). Punter Brunno Reus is averaging 44.47 yards a kick and has stopped 18 of 47 punts inside the opponent’s 20-yard line. Punt returner DaMarion Fowlkes averaged 10 yards a return and had a 68-yard TD vs. Troy. As a kickoff returner, Fowlkes is averaging 24.8 yards on 12 returns. I know rivalry games can make records look meaningless, and the Golden Bears would love nothing more than to keep their neighbors out of a bowl game. But at some point, I have to back the team that's actually moving in the right direction. Stanford has won three of its last four, while Cal has lost four straight and looks completely out of answers under Tosh Lupoi. The Cardinal can become bowl eligible for the first time since 2018, and I think they're playing with the urgency to make that happen. What's changed for Stanford is that the offense finally has something it can lean on. Micah Ford has rushed for at least 145 yards in three of the last four games, and he's averaging 137.5 rushing yards since the win over Elon. He just ran for 149 yards and three touchdowns in a 40-22 victory at Virginia Tech. That's a big deal against a Cal defense allowing 186.2 rushing yards per game. Stanford hasn't been a great rushing team over the entire season, but Ford's recent form gives the Cardinal a way to control possessions instead of asking Davis Warren to do everything. Warren has quietly done a nice job protecting the football. He's thrown for 2,406 yards with 14 touchdowns and only three interceptions, despite ranking among the national leaders in pass attempts. Stanford is still converting just 31.7 percent of its third downs, so it's not as though every offensive problem has disappeared. But when you can get the running game going and avoid handing the opponent short fields, you give yourself a much better chance to win close games. That's been missing from this program for a while. Cal's offense is the bigger concern for me. The Bears are scoring just 20.4 points per game and averaging only 78.7 rushing yards. That's an awful lot of pressure on Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele, who's thrown 11 touchdowns against eight interceptions. Chase Hendricks has been productive with 65 catches, but defenses don't have to respect the run nearly enough. Cal managed seven points at Virginia last week, and that loss followed defeats to Wake Forest , SMU and NC State. Those four losses have come by at least three touchdowns apiece. That's not a team that's simply catching a few unlucky breaks. I won't pretend Stanford is some defensive powerhouse. The Cardinal allow 35.8 points and nearly 449 yards per game, numbers that give Cal a legitimate opportunity to move the ball. But Stanford forced three turnovers against Virginia Tech, with Charlie Eckhardt recording two interceptions and a forced fumble. That was the Cardinal's first road win since 2024, snapping a 15-game skid away from home. The defense doesn't suddenly become great because of one afternoon, but there are signs of improvement when the offense gives it a chance. The travel angle is another reason I don't mind the road favorite here. Stanford has been crushed on several cross-country trips since joining the ACC, but going from Palo Alto to Berkeley is hardly the same situation. Cal also returns home after three straight road games, so maybe getting back to its own building helps. They haven't played in Berkeley since October 17, so there's some uncertainty there. The Bears have won the last two Big Games played in Berkeley, and that matters in a rivalry. Stanford, though, took back the Axe with a 31-10 win last season. Now there's a bowl bid waiting on the other side of another rivalry victory, while Cal is already eliminated from postseason consideration. Chris Ruffolo's Pick: Stanford -2.5 Need More? away.blurb: Although there are no new Cal players listed as being out, four starters are listed as questionable. Starting wide receiver Ian Strong, who missed last week's game, as well as defensive back Daniel Harris, safety Isaiah Crosby and inside linebacker JD McKinley are the four Cal starters listed as questionable. Safety Aiden Manutai, outside linebacker Justin Beadles and defensive lineman Ashun Shepphard are also Cal players expected to get playing time if they are healthy, but all three are listed as questionable. Also of interest is the fact that quarterback Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele and running back Adam Mohammed are listed as probable. That indicates they are likely to play against Stanford, but it also suggests they are nursing some injuries. Three Cal players listed as being out for the Big Game are the same players who have been sidelined for virtually the entire season -- running back Carter Vargas, defensive lineman Nate Burrell and tight end Dorian Thomas. Crosby is second on the team in tackles with 56 and he also has an interception and two tackles for loss. Harris is fifth on the team in tackles with 37, and he also has three tackles for loss and four quarterback hurries. Cal is 3-7 overall and is riding a four-game losing streak. The Bears will host Stanford (5-5, 4-5 ACC) in Saturday's Big Game starting at 4:30 p.m. The Cardinal would become bowl-eligible if it beats Cal. (Photo by Patrick Mulligan/Getty Images) (Patrick Mulligan/Getty Images) Delayna Zepeda · Dallas Morning News Thu, November 19, 2026 at 12:00 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads No. 2 Utah at TCU 8 p.m. Saturday at Amon G. Carter Stadium, Fort Worth TCU (5–5, 3–4 Big 12), Utah (10–0, 7–0) TCU defeated Utah on the road in 2024, 13-7 What's at stake? The TCU Horned Frogs will face one of their toughest challenges of the season Saturday when they host No. 2 Utah at Amon G. Carter Stadium. The Frogs are coming off a 20-10 victory over Kansas State , while the Utes enter the matchup looking to keep their undefeated season alive. Utah is 10-0 overall and 7-0 in Big 12 play. Saturday's matchup will mark the highest-ranked opponent to visit Amon G. Carter Stadium since No. 2 Texas in 1970. It also marks TCU's final home game of the season before the Frogs travel to face Texas Tech on Thanksgiving Day. With a win, TCU would secure bowl eligibility and pull off one of the biggest upsets of the college football season. When TCU has the ball Quarterback Jaden Craig will be a key factor in TCU's ability to keep up with Utah's offense. Craig has thrown for 2,664 yards, 13 touchdowns and seven interceptions this season. He is coming off a 225-yard performance against Kansas State, where he also threw a touchdown pass. The Horned Frogs will need to find ways to create offensive opportunities without relying entirely on Craig's arm. Establishing the run game and finding success on early downs will be important against a Utah defense that has helped the Utes remain undefeated. Craig has also been dealing with an ankle injury that has limited his mobility. However, head coach Sonny Dykes said during Tuesday's midweek news conference that Craig is showing improvement and is expected to play Saturday. "I would expect him to play. He was a lot better today than he was yesterday. I would anticipate him being able to practice tomorrow and play on Saturday," Dykes said Tuesday. TCU will need to sustain drives, limit mistakes and take advantage of its scoring opportunities if it hopes to pull off the upset. The Frogs showed they can do that with their 20-10 victory over Kansas State. When Kansas State has the ball Undefeated Utah has been one of the strongest teams in the Big 12 this season and is looking to secure a spot in the conference championship game. picks.blurb: No. 2 Utah Looks to Stay Perfect Against TCU: Week 12 Preview - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football CFP And Bowl Games Commanders stun Bengals Florida State hires new coach MLB players' union blasts proposal Will SEC boot LSU? Week 12 Waiver Wire No. 2 Utah Looks to Stay Perfect Against TCU: Week 12 Preview (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect) Sam LeSueur · Roundtable Sports Sat, November 21, 2026 at 8:27 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads No. 2 Utah (10-0, 7-0 Big 12) heads to Fort Worth to take on TCU (5-5, 3-4 Big 12) in its final road game of the regular season. Coming off a 40-39 victory over Arizona , Utah has an opportunity to improve to 11-0 and secure its spot in the Big 12 Championship Game. One matchup that stands out is Utah's rushing defense against TCU's rushing offense. The Utes lead the Big 12 in rushing defense, allowing just 98.9 yards per game, while TCU ranks last in the conference in rushing offense at 106.5 yards per game. Even with leading rusher Jeremy Payne returning from injury last week, TCU managed just 99 rushing yards against Kansas State. Here are four keys to a Utah victory. Play Tight Man Coverage and Bring Constant Pressure Utah needs to be aggressive defensively from the opening possession. TCU has allowed 28 sacks this season, and its offensive line has struggled in pass protection. The Utes should play tight man-to-man coverage, get physical with TCU's bigger receivers and tight ends at the line of scrimmage, and bring consistent pressure. There will be some risk involved, and TCU could connect on a few explosive plays. However, I believe the reward outweighs the risk. Utah has the defensive personnel to make life difficult for TCU's offense, and consistent pressure should create opportunities for sacks and interceptions. Run a Balanced Offense TCU has one of the better defenses in the Big 12, allowing just 304.4 total yards per game. However, Kansas and Arizona both found success moving the football against the Horned Frogs by maintaining a balanced attack. Kansas finished with 451 total yards, including 285 passing and 166 rushing. Arizona recorded 441 yards, with 313 passing and 128 rushing. Utah is averaging 223.6 rushing yards and 247.8 passing yards per game. The Utes have the ability to attack TCU both on the ground and through the air. Keeping the play-calling balanced and utilizing Devon Dampier's dual-threat ability should prevent TCU from focusing on stopping one aspect of Utah's offense. Hold On to the Football One of TCU's biggest defensive strengths is its ability to force fumbles. The Horned Frogs have forced 12 fumbles this season and recovered eight. Kylin Jackson and Koron Hayward have combined for seven forced fumbles alone. TCU's defenders are aggressive when attacking the football, particularly when runners are fighting for extra yards. Utah needs to make ball security a priority throughout the game. TCU's defense is good enough to keep this game competitive, and giving the Horned Frogs extra possessions could make things much more difficult than they need to be. Rattle TCU's New Starting Quarterback With Jaden Craig doubtful due to an ankle injury, TCU is expected to start Adam Schobel, who would be making his first career start. Schobel has attempted just one pass this season, and Utah needs to take advantage of that inexperience. The Utes should bring pressure early, disguise coverages, and force Schobel into difficult third-down situations. Utah cannot allow an inexperienced quarterback to get comfortable with easy completions and extended drives. If the Utes can shut down TCU's rushing attack and force Schobel to beat them through the air, I like Utah's chances of creating turnovers and controlling this game defensively. Final Score Prediction No. 2 Utah 34, TCU 7 TCU's defense will present some challenges, but I believe Utah has too many weapons offensively. The Utes should be able to shut down TCU's struggling rushing attack, put consistent pressure on its inexperienced quarterback, and control the game. Utah improves to 11-0 and secures its spot in the Big 12 Championship Game .
